source_review.notes: Checked all ten references. Current POSIX.1-2024 mutex behavior; Java SE 26 Lock blocking, interruptible, timed, try, condition, ordering, and memory semantics plus ReentrantLock fairness and barging; and current Rust 1.98 and Go mutex contracts were verified against official specifications.

notation_and_syntax.notes: Graph, hierarchy, progress, timeout, and recovery concepts remain distinct.

evidence: Executed all 36 pairs of two-lock orders over three locks and independently confirmed 6 reversed cyclic pairs; the 9 globally increasing pairs contain zero reversals.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Counts match exact stdout and the stated finite direct-cycle model.

evidence: Re-derived the strict-rank contradiction around a cycle, Coffman-condition prevention choices, dynamic-set canonicalization, upgrade cycle, and try-lock rollback boundary.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The theorem explicitly assumes every relevant dependency participates in one stable strict order.

boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Normal and abnormal paths use the same global dependency discipline.

evidence: Checked strict upward acquisition, stable rank/key lifetime, matched guard ownership, reverse unwind, complete pre-acquisition canonicalization, open-call revalidation, no hidden wait, and quiescent destruction.
invariant_checking.notes: Prevention claims remain scoped to modeled dependencies and do not imply fairness.

evidence: Reviewed rank theorem line by line, two-lock wait graph, dynamic-key counterexample, callback-hidden edge, reader-upgrade deadlock, join cycle, and recovery authority.
proof_review.notes: Prevention, avoidance, detection, recovery, timeout, livelock, starvation, and priority inversion are not conflated.

evidence: Audited the dynamic lock-set schema, formal rank proof, wait-graph claims, API-specific try/fairness behavior, and safety-critical boundary.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The schema is explicitly non-executable and API claims are version-scoped.

empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Evidence disclaims real threads, longer cycles, modes, callbacks, queues, conditions, fairness, cancellation, and arbitrary deadlock freedom.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, practitioner, railway, medical-device, clinical, real-time, controls, hardware, functional-safety, cybersecurity, regulatory, quality, or human-factors review is claimed. Finite enumeration, source checking, and manual analysis do not prove arbitrary program deadlock freedom, fairness, timing, rollback safety, or safety-critical deployment fitness.
